FR-001.title: The die step is a search page accepting a die (FGT) number or a part number and reads no job.

FR-002.title: A die number is accepted only when Infor Visual records it; a miss is refused naming Infor Visual and the flow does not advance.

FR-003.title: A part-number search returns every die Visual associates with that part, explicit association first and work-order history completing the list.

FR-004.title: A typed die number is normalised the way the existing part search normalises a term.

FR-005.title: An unreachable Infor Visual is reported with the attempt time and a retry, keeping the requester's term.

FR-006.title: Each die is listed with its own location, and a die with none says so instead of drawing an empty cell.

FR-007.title: The number of matches is visible so a partial list cannot pass for a complete one.

FR-008.title: Every match is reachable however many there are.

FR-009.title: A die whose description is the plant's placeholder shows that text as its description, never as a location.

FR-010.title: The requester can choose one die or several, and the chosen dies stay marked when results are revisited.

FR-011.title: Each chosen die becomes its own request and the confirmation step lists every one of them.

FR-012.title: Each resulting card names its own die and that die's location.

FR-013.title: Choosing no die does not advance the flow.

FR-014.title: The Temp preview source behind the die search page and the die card variant are deleted and the build stays green.

intent: Give the generic request flow a live Infor Visual die search that lists every die a part owns with locations and raises one request per chosen die.

concerns.note: The four dispatch-briefs readers could not run: the DeepSeek provider returned 402 monthly quota exceeded. The plan was grounded by reading the same files inline instead.
The plant SQL Server (VISUAL/MTMFG) is unreachable from this workstation, so GetDieSearch.sql was never executed against live data; it is written to the exported schema in docs/database only.

decisions.decision: Find a part's dies from PART_ALTERNATE first and complete the list from the part's work-order REQUIREMENT history, deduplicated by die number.
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for exactly that precedence; PART_ALTERNATE is the only exported table that records a deliberate part-to-part association, and the requirement history is what the work-order flow already reads as a part's dies.
decisions.rejected: PART_SUBSTITUTE (like-for-like material, not tooling) and a description match over FGT parts (invents associations).

decisions.decision: A normalised term starting with FGT is a die number matched exactly; every other term is a part number, also tried once as an FGT-prefixed die number.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for the existing part-search normalisation, and FR-002 needs a typed die number that exists nowhere to be refused rather than silently answered as a part search.
decisions.rejected: Treating every term as both a die number and a part number, which would answer a misspelled die with another part's dies.

decisions.decision: A die's location is PART_SITE.PRIMARY_LOC_ID, then the lowest PART_LOCATION.LOCATION_ID, then no location at all.
decisions.why: GetSubordinateParts.sql already resolves a die this way and records that quantity ranking is meaningless for a die; ordering the fallback by location id keeps it deterministic.
decisions.rejected: The highest-quantity stock row, which is the rule the subordinate query replaced.

decisions.decision: Each result row carries its own IsSelected toggled by a tap, with a visible count above the list, matching the New Request die step.
decisions.why: FR-010 needs one or several chosen and still marked when results are revisited, and a multiple-selection ListView cannot be two-way bound without code-behind.
decisions.rejected: ListView.SelectedItems read in code-behind, which would be a second source of truth beside the draft.

decisions.decision: Raising a die request walks the chosen dies and raises one request per die, storing die.number and die.location in the request's answers; the card reads them for a generic request.
decisions.why: FR-011 and FR-012: the queue separates entries by the captured value, and a generic request has no job for the board to resolve a die from.
decisions.rejected: One request carrying several dies (the duplicate rule would collapse them) and resolving the location on the board (a read per card).

decisions.decision: The die read gets its own seam, IGenericRequestDieData, implemented in MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest.Data and delegated to from GenericRequestLiveStepData; the Die step reports Ready.
decisions.why: The part step already established a read with its own seam and tests, and GenericRequestLiveStepData is the flow's delegating seam for every other step.
decisions.rejected: Implementing the Visual SQL inside GenericRequestLiveStepData, which carries no Visual knowledge today.

decisions.decision: The search shows a die's own description exactly as Visual records it, including 'Die still needs location', and never reads it as a location.
decisions.why: FR-009 says so; on a job the same text means 'this job has no die', which is a different question from a search hit.
decisions.rejected: Filtering placeholder-described dies out of the results, which would hide a die the plant records.

decisions.decision: The die search is live only: no read shape and no mtm_mock mirror.
decisions.why: Spec A4 and the FR-084 precedent for the incorrect-part search: an association search is not a mirrorable shape, and the app never refreshes the mirror.
decisions.rejected: Adding a sixth read shape, which would mirror three Visual tables.

decisions.decision: Normalise with PartMatchSearchInput and add a project reference from MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest.Data to MTM_Waitlist.Waitlist.NewRequest
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for the identical normalisation, so the one class that owns it is shared rather than copied
decisions.rejected: a second copy of the padding rule in the die read

decisions.decision: Keep the chosen dies in the view model and write them to the draft on Continue
decisions.why: a re-search must not drop a choice, and the draft is only written when the requester leaves the step

decisions.decision: Stop the raise walk at the first failed write and say how many landed
decisions.why: a failure proves nothing about the remaining dies, and a retry that silently re-raises the successful ones would duplicate them
decisions.rejected: continuing past a failure and reporting only successes

plan.summary: Plan, research and design artifacts for a live Infor Visual die search that lists every die a part owns and raises one request per chosen die.
plan.key_finding: The die card cannot resolve a location for a generic request because there is no job, so the die's location must be stored on the request's own answers.

tasks.summary: 31 tasks in six phases: setup wording, a foundational read/raise phase, one phase per user story, and Polish.

implement.summary: The die step now answers from a live Infor Visual search, lists every die a part owns with its location, and raises one request per chosen die with the die answer stored for the card.

approach: Add a checked-in GetDieSearch.sql that answers dies by die number, PART_ALTERNATE association or work-order requirement history, run it through a new IGenericRequestDieData seam behind the existing step seam, let the page choose one or several dies with a visible count, and raise one request per chosen die with die.number and die.location stored on its answers so the card can name both.
